SHANGHAI, 23 May 1934.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY. No D. 2702 Date 24 / 5 / 34）

Sir,

Further to my letter of 10 March 1932 No. 725 (your number D. 2702/1932) I have the honour to inform you that I am in receipt of a communication from Hongkong to the effect that Ludwig Adler, at the time suspected to be an agent of the Komintern, appears to employ tactics in commercial matters which almost amount to swindling.

In 1933 he received a consignement of goods from the "N.V. Electrotechn. Mechan. Industrie" at Utrecht (Holland) for an amount of £ 151.17.3, which soon after arrival was auctioned by his orders, without the proceeds being ever remitted to his principal.

He has left Hongkong for Europe, travelling probably via Siberia.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
（签名）
Chinese Secretary.

T. Robertson, Esquire,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
Special Branch,

SHANGHAI, 22nd October 1931.

Sir,

I have the honour to inform you that according to infor-
mation received Ludwig Adler, left Singapore on the 19th of
September by the s.s. "Kashmir" for Hongkong.

He seems to have abandoned his plans for a trip to Nether-
lands India "for business reasons".

He arrived in Hongkong on 24 September 1931 and stayed
at the Peninsula Hotel until the 26th of that month.

He registered at Police Headquarters in Hongkong of his
own accord on the 2nd of October, stating in conversation that
he was an old "China hand", who had been visiting the Far East
as a commercial traveller for the past 28 years.

He appears to represent the following concerns:

1. Messrs. T.A. Cockin, Ltd., Manufacturers of Asbestos goods
of Huddersfield, Yorkshire, England.

2. Messrs. Craye & Fils, Tapestry and furniture covering
manufacturers, of Roubaix, North France.

He also represents several small Czecho-Slovakian concerns.

It appears to be his intention to make Hongkong his business
headquarters in the near future and to rent an office there.

At the present time he is staying at 292 Prince Edward Road,
the residence of Mr. Komor of Messrs. Komor & Komor, who he
says, is a very old friend of his.

His presence in Hongkong so far has given no rise to
suspicions.

He is short and stout build, clean shaven, has a small
nose and a healthy complexion. He speaks almost faultless
English.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

Deputy Commissioner of Police,
Crime & Special Branches,

SHANGHAI.

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O. BOX 280. SHANGHAI.
21st September 1931.

PERSONAL.

Dear Mr Robertson,

With reference to No.S.B-D2703 of
26.8.31 from Mr.Givens to Mr. Steptoe, the following
message was received this morning from Singapore:-
"Ludvig ADLER leaving for Hongkong by s.s.Kashmir 20th
September. Hongkong not informed. He has given no
cause for suspicion here".

If you think Hongkong should be advised
about Adler's movements you will no doubt take the
necessary steps.
I shall very much appreciate if in due
course you could confirm or refute the French report that
this man is a Communist agent.

Yours sincerely,
[Signature]

H.Robertson, Esq.,
(Special Branch)
C.I.D.

H.R

Special Branch,
August 31, 1931.

S. 2.

Re Addler

Information is received that Addler is travelling on
Czecho-Slovakian Passport No. 7/378/1929 issued at
Shanghai on March 6, 1929 and vised by the police in
Paris on October 4, 1930. The Singapore Police have
telegraphed to say that they have no ground for suspicion
against him but that he intends going to Java. Please
see the Netherlands Consular Authorities and ask them if
it is possible to keep a watch on his movements while in
Java and to let us know immediately he leaves that port.

Henry Robertson
C.D.I.

D.S. Makinson
a track & file.
J.S.R.
31/8.

Special Branch,
August 28, 1931.

S. 2.

Adler has reached Singapore. S. will
endeavour to keep us posted about his further
movements. However S. 2 should keep a watch in
co-operation with the Chinese Passport Authorities
and French Police for his arrival. When Adler
arrives, S.2 should keep a watch on his movements,
but should refrain from doing anything likely to
lead him to suspect that he is under surveillance.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
C. & S. I. RECORDS
No. S. B. D. 2702.
Date 26 - 8 - 31.

August 26 31.

My dear Steptoe,

The following radio has been received by
the French Consular Authorities from Indo-China :-

"Ludvig ADLER, born at Gratemichal, Checco-Slovakia,
"on August 25th, 1878, resides usually in Vienna,
"Austria. Reported to be an important agent of
"the III International in China as well as in
"French and British colonies of the Pacific.
"Supposed to have resided in Shanghai in 1920-
"1922 and in 1927. Passed through Indo-China in
"1928. End 1928 - 1929 Moscow.
"Reported to have left Juan-les-Pins (France) on
"the 26th July 1931 for Genoa, from where he
"intends to proceed to Singapore.
"Description : Age about fifty, tall, hair light
"brown, rather thin, heavily built, clean shaven,
"small nose, 'American type'".

Yours sincerely,

H.N. Steptoe, Esq.,
H.B.M. Consulate-General.

TRANSLATION

Ludvig ADLER, born at Gratemichal, Checo-Slovakia, on
August 25th 1875. Resides usually in Vienna, Austria. .
Reported to be an important agent of the III International
in China as well as in French and British colonies of the
Pacific. Supposed to have resided in Shanghai in 1920 -
1922 and in 1927. Passed through Indo-China in 1928.
End 1928 - 1929 - Moscow.
Reported to have left Juan-les-Pins (France) on the 26th
July 1931 for Genua, from where he intends to proceed
to Singapore.

    Age about fifty; tall; hair light brown, rather thin;
heavely built;clean shaven; small noze; "American type".
